title: Reduce packed-support decode overhead with one adaptive byte-table path
question: Can the existing packed Boolean support decoder perform less Python-level work per set bit while retaining exact sorted canonical CSR support, bounded refusal semantics, and the existing TypedRelationBlock authority boundary?

change.reuse: Change the existing experiments.tensor_gpu.cpu_bitset_baseline._csr_support_from_masks helper in place; do not add another materialization module or benchmark harness.
change.sparse_path: Retain the existing lowest-set-bit walk for sparse output rows.
change.dense_path: For denser rows, scan a fixed-width little-endian int.to_bytes view and reuse one immutable 256-entry byte-to-bit-offset lookup table, preserving strictly increasing canonical column order.
change.crossover: Choose the byte path when mask.bit_count() exceeds half of the encoded row byte width; this decision depends only on admitted row geometry and observed support density.
change.entry_bound: Use mask.bit_count() to preflight cumulative MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES before decoding a row and retain the existing refusal message.
change.semantic_control: The unchanged CSR BooleanSemiring oracle, TypedRelationBlock output, subject, axes, support and canonical digest remain the correctness controls.

frozen_current_run_diagnostic.measurement_caveat: These are one hosted-run diagnostics. GPU-14 numbers came from a different hosted run, so before/after wall-time deltas across packets are not a controlled A/B benchmark and do not mint a speedup claim.

finding.summary: The existing decoder can reduce per-entry Python work on dense rows without changing the semantic surface. In this run the 43,264-entry profile case spends 1.649411 ms in support decode versus 9.594229 ms in canonical construction, while all six cases preserve exact support and digest.
finding.negative_result: The experiment does not justify a new decoder subsystem, cache, trusted constructor, backend, or broad performance claim. Sparse rows still use the simpler original bit walk.
finding.next_implication: After this bounded decoder change, canonical TypedRelationBlock construction again dominates the dense-output materialization boundary in this run. A later packet may investigate that existing boundary, but this packet performs no further abstraction or promotion.
